headline: Watch Cheetah Mom Zura Care for 5 Newborn Cubs Live
meta_description: A live webcam at the Smithsonian's Conservation Institute lets you watch cheetah Zura nurture her five cubs born in October—and listen to their purrs and chirp…
summary_short: Five cheetah cubs born at Virginia's Smithsonian facility are now visible 24/7 on a live feed, offering rare insight into maternal care and conservation efforts.
body:
On October 5, a cheetah named Zura gave birth to five cubs at the Smithsonian's Conservation Institute in Front Royal, Virginia—and the facility has opened a live webcam window into their den for the public to watch around the clock. The camera captures not just the visual intimacy of Zura tending her newborns, but also the acoustic landscape of the nursery: soft chirps, tiny purrs, and meows as the cubs nurse, groom, and wrestle with one another. It's a rare glimpse into wild animal behavior that most people never experience.

What makes this moment especially significant is the conservation context behind it. Cheetahs face critical challenges in the wild, with fewer than 7,000 individuals remaining globally. Cubs born at this facility grow up with minimal human contact early in their lives—unlike animals at the nearby Washington, DC zoo—which allows them to bond more naturally with their mother while enabling researchers to conduct behavioral studies impossible in traditional zoo settings. The same camera feed used by caretakers for remote monitoring now serves a dual purpose: allowing the public to witness the meticulous work of species preservation.

Tuning in to Zura's den isn't simply heartwarming entertainment. It's a window into the infrastructure of survival—the dedicated effort to ensure cheetahs have a future beyond extinction. Visitors to the Smithsonian's webpage can watch the cubs develop and learn about the broader conservation mission, with the option to support the work directly through donations.
quick_facts: Zura gave birth to five cheetah cubs on October 5 at Smithsonian facility
Located in Front Royal, Virginia, the facility provides 24/7 live webcam access
Fewer than 7,000 cheetahs remain in the wild today
Cubs receive minimal human contact to strengthen mother-cub bonding
